name: Hoanh thanh
summary: Hoi An’s wonton, filled with shrimp or with shrimp and pork, three ways: fried crisp under a tomato sauce, in a clear pork-bone broth, or on thin wheat noodles.
origin: Hoi An. The Hoi An World Heritage conservation centre’s 28 June 2011 article, citing vntravellive.com, calls it a Chinese port dish. Quảng Nam says hoành thánh. The same article says some northern speakers say mằn thắn or vằn thắn. It also prints a Qianlong naming story and does not cite a document for that story.
howToEat: The 2011 article gives three plates. Soup: seven to ten dumplings in a clear pork-bone broth with straw mushrooms, cabbage, and pineapple, plus satay and crushed fried pork crackling. Eat it with a lot of broth.
Fried: folded square, on lettuce, tomato, and Trà Quế herbs, with a tomato-and-potato sauce.
Noodles: thin wheat noodles, blanched, with the dumplings and the same broth. Eat them hot.

The centre’s 4 September 2024 article, republishing Dân Việt, says a shrimp-and-pork filling, with pork liver, garlic chives, and a soft-yolk egg, or a fried plate with chili sauce. The 2011 filling is land shrimp. Both stay.
seoDescription: Hoành thánh in Hoi An is fried, in a pork-bone broth, or on thin noodles. One article fills it with shrimp. Another adds pork.
